text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- GOVT LIMITS IMPORT FINANCING, CONSUMER GOODS BADLY HIT

Brazil introduced new rules to limit the attractiveness of short-term import financing in an attempt to correct a gaping trade deficit. Central Bank International Affairs director said most importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they retreive their goods from customs.
-- BAMERINDUS CLOSE TO A FINAL SOLUTION
Bamerindus stock fell 6.9 percent on Tuesday following strong rumors that the bank's shareholders were close to reaching a final solution for the confidence problems that have plagued the bank.
-- FORMER MALUF ALLY SAYS PITTA IS A MERE FRONTMAN

Joao Carlos Martins, accused of illegally raising $19 million for former mayor Paulo Maluf's election campaign funds, said current mayor Celso Pitta was a mere frontman for Maluf. Pitta is under investigation by a congressional probe and is being accused of profiting from a multi-million dollar bond scam.
-- GOVERNMENT TAKES ACTION TO RESTRICT IMPORTS
The Brazilian government took new action to contain imports finananced over a period of less than 360 days. Importers will be required to pay in full for the merchandise when it arrives arrives.
-- CONGRESSIONAL PROBE SUSPECTS RIO BOND ISSUE
A congressional probe investigating the illegal bond issues suspects several of the banks involved in the multi-million dollar scam also traded Rio de Janeiro's so-called "carioquinha" bonds.
-- WOMAN KILLED BY STRAY BULLET IN RIO SHOOT-OUT

A woman who was shopping in Rio de Janeiro's Ipanema neighborhood on Tuesday afternoon was hit by a stray bullet and died en route to the hospital, after police exchanged shots with six thieves who were holding up a bank. Five of the thieves escaped. One was captured.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
